problems.problem: The reading lists the births as 'the fire beneath the ocean, the sun in heaven and the lightning in mid-air' directly under a key verse that prints 'in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters'. Griffith's 'mid-air' renders samudra, which Sāyaṇa takes as the ocean, and Griffith's 'waters' renders apsu, which Sāyaṇa takes as a name of mid-air (āpaḥ iti antarikṣanāma). Read beside the key, the sentence seems to put the lightning where the verse puts mid-air and to drop the waters, so a reader cannot square the two and it looks like an error.
problems.fix: Make the mapping explicit from his own gloss, for example: '...; Sāyaṇa, on 1.95.3, reads them as the fire beneath the ocean, the sun in heaven and the lightning, taking ‘the waters’ as a name for mid-air.' (the seasons clause can go to keep the cap).

problems.problem: 'the time of their first creation being no time at all' means in idiomatic English that the waters were created instantly. Sāyaṇa means the opposite: kim is used in dismissal, the time has no measure because there was no first creation, the waters being eternal (na kim api; nityā eva hi tāḥ).
problems.fix: '...; Sāyaṇa, on 2.30.1, takes the question as a dismissal, since the waters are eternal and there was no first time to measure.'

problems.problem: 'reads the sins as debts, his forebears’ and his own': the nearest antecedent of 'his' is Sāyaṇa, so the sentence says Sāyaṇa's forebears. His gloss is the debts made by the speaker's fathers (pitrādibhiḥ kṛtāni) and those the speaker made himself.
problems.fix: 'reads the sins as debts, the singer’s forebears’ and his own, and the undawned mornings as dawns that seem not to break for a debtor awake before daylight.' (45 words)

problems.problem: 'sent after the cows the Paṇis stole once Indra promised their milk to her young' parses as the Paṇis stealing the cows once Indra promised; in Sāyaṇa's tale the theft comes first and Saramā agrees to go only when Indra promises her young the cows' milk.
problems.fix: '...; Sāyaṇa, on 1.62.3, reads it through the tale of Sarama, the gods’ hound, sent after the cows the Paṇis stole, and going only once Indra promised their milk to her young.'

problems.problem: 'the hymn turns to its length' reads as the length of the hymn, not the length of the life just mentioned; the context clause is unclear at the one point it has to carry.
problems.fix: Replace with 'the hymn names that life’s span' (or similar wording that ties the length to the life), keeping 45 words or fewer.

problems.problem: 'the Maruts as serving men in the form of breath' can be read as the Maruts being serving-men (servants); Sāyaṇa glosses nṛṣācaḥ as attending on men in the form of breath (prāṇarūpeṇa nṝn sevamānāḥ). The context clause 'turns to the praise and the Maruts' is also vague: which praise is not said.
problems.fix: '...and the Maruts as attending on men in the form of breath.' and a context clause such as 'In a hymn on Indra’s fight with Vrtra, the verse tells of the singers’ hymn and the Maruts’ joy' within the 45-word cap.

problems.problem: Doubled word in one clause: 'which names Agni as each god in turn, this verse turns to the gods'.
problems.fix: 'In the book’s opening hymn, which names Agni as each god in turn, the verse speaks of the gods; ...'

problems.problem: The sentence spells the god 'Vishnu' twice directly under a key verse that prints 'Visnu' (Griffith's spelling), and day 20 of the same batch writes 'Visnu'. The reader sees two spellings of one name on one card and across the batch.
problems.fix: Write 'Visnu' in both places, as the key verse and day 20 print it.

problems.problem: Batch prose: 15 of 32 context clauses use the same formula 'the hymn/verse/singer turns to ...' (days 2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19, 22, 26, 32), including an unbroken run from day 7 to day 14; read morning after morning it becomes a tic and blunts clauses that should say what the passage is doing.
problems.fix: Vary the context clauses on at least half of these days with the passage's own action (asks, answers, tells of, pleads, names, closes on), keeping each within the passage and under the cap; days 7, 11 and 26 are fixed above.
